methodology: Multilayer nanofibrous membranes were fabricated by electrospinning polyacrylonitrile (PAN), chitosan (CS), and Nylon6 (N6). Morphological and mechanical properties were evaluated using SEM and tensile testing, while adsorption experiments were conducted with synthetic and real river water samples.
research_objective: To engineer and optimize multilayer electrospun nanofibrous membranes for the removal of hexavalent chromium and cadmium from water matrices.

key_findings.finding: Multilayer electrospun nanofibrous membranes based on PAN, CS, and N6 achieve high adsorption efficiency for Cr6+ and Cd2+ in both synthetic and real river water samples.

The combination of high adsorption efficiency, mechanical stability, and effectiveness in real water matrices validate the use of multilayer electrospun membranes as a robust and environmentally friendly method for water purification applications.
Electrospinning-based manufacturing of nanostructured membranes has shown great promise in the development of water purification technologies.
Functional polymers such as chitosan, PAA, and PEI have demonstrated high adsorption capacities for heavy metal ions including Cu2+, Pb2+, Cd2+, and Cr6+.
The proposed gauze-based collectorsubstrate enabled the formation of continuous, defect-free CS fibers.

The hierarchical architecture combined with a tailored fiber collection strategy allowed the membrane to harness the complementary properties of each polymer: PAN for antimicrobial activity, chitosan for strong affinity toward heavy metal ions, and Nylon6 for structural robustness and water stability.

The membranes successfully demonstrated effective heavy metal removal capacity along with high mechanical stability, confirming their significant potential for use in sustainable water treatment applications.

Conclusions ElectrospunmembranesweresuccessfullyfabricatedusingpolymersolutionsofPAN, CS,andN6atvariousconcentrations. Theoptimalconcentrationsforproducinghomo- geneous fibers were determined to be 12 wt% for PAN, 2 wt% for CS, and 22 wt% for N6. The CS membranes exhibited an average fiber diameter of d = 0.12±0.306 µm f andamechanicalstrengthof0.12MPa. Incomparison,PANandN6fibershadaverage diametersof0.245±0.07µmand0.14±0.03µm,withcorrespondingmechanicalstrengths of1.89MPaand2.1MPa,respectively. TheincorporationofPANandN6notablyenhanced thestructuralstabilityandmechanicalperformanceofthemultilayermembranes. Theadsorptioncapacityofthemembraneswasassessedusingbothsyntheticwater samplescontaining2mg/Lofchromiumandcadmium,andnaturalriverwatersamples fromtheCutuchiRiver,whichincludedorganiccontaminants. Allsixmultilayerconfigura- tionsdemonstratedhighremovalefficienciesinsynthetictests,reachingupto78.98%for Cd2+ and80.81%forCr6+. Basedontheseresults,membranesM5(CS/PAN/N6)andM6 (CS/N6/PAN)wereselectedforfurtherevaluationwithnaturalwatersamples.
